title: Number of Squareful Arrays
summary: An array is considered squareful if the sum of any two adjacent elements is a perfect square.
statement: An array is considered squareful if the sum of any two adjacent elements is a perfect square. Given an integer array, determine the count of distinct permutations where each pair of adjacent elements sums to a perfect square.
constraints: Count distinct permutations where every adjacent sum is a perfect square.
Duplicate input values must not duplicate the count.
hints: Backtrack over remaining value frequencies rather than positions to avoid duplicate permutations.
A candidate may follow previous only when their sum is a perfect square.
Decrement its count, recurse, restore, and return one when no positions remain.
Each distinct value sequence chooses one frequency branch at every depth exactly once.
editorial: Each distinct value sequence chooses one frequency branch at every depth exactly once.

tests.explanation: The valid distinct orders are 1,8,17 and 17,8,1.
The only distinct permutation is valid because 2+2=4.
